questions.text:
Nitrogen dioxide gas is almost twice as dense as nitrogen gas. A gas jar of nitrogen dioxide was placed on top of a gas jar of nitrogen gas with the open ends together. After half an hour, which of these statements would be true?

A  Both gases would not have mixed.
B  The bottom gas jar contained nitrogen gas only.
C  The top gas jar contained nitrogen dioxide gas only.
D  Some of each gas would have moved into the other gas jar.

The diagram shows the apparatus used to separate hexane (boiling point 70 °C) and water.

[DIAGRAM – DISTILLATION APPARATUS AND FOUR GRAPHS]
Distillation apparatus with flask, condenser, and collection flask. Point T marked at the top of the condenser.
Four graphs (A–D) show temperature/°C on y-axis (range 70–100) against 'total volume of distillate' on x-axis.
Graph A: starts at 70, stays flat, jumps to 100 and stays flat (two plateaus — correct).
Graph B: starts at 100, stays flat, drops to 70 and stays flat.
Graph C: rises linearly from 70 to 100.
Graph D: falls linearly from 100 to 70.
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

Which graph would be obtained if the temperature at point T was plotted against the total volume of distillate collected?

A  graph A
B  graph B
C  graph C
D  graph D

A student titrated 25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide with hydrochloric acid. The diagram shows the volume of hydrochloric acid in the burette at the start and the end of the titration.

[DIAGRAM – TWO BURETTE READINGS]
Left burette (start): meniscus at approximately 1.20 cm³.
Right burette (end): meniscus at approximately 30.80 cm³.
Burettes have markings from 0 (top) to 32+ (bottom).
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

What volume of hydrochloric acid was added from the burette?

A  29.00 cm³
B  29.60 cm³
C  31.30 cm³
D  32.70 cm³

The formulae of the ions of some elements are shown below:

P³⁻   S²⁻   Cl⁻   Li⁺   Mg²⁺

Which of the following statements about these ions is correct?

A  They all have more electrons than protons.
B  They all have the same number of electron shells.
C  They all have the same number of neutrons in their nuclei.
D  They all have the same electronic structures as noble gases.

Elements X and Y form an ionic compound of formula X₃Y. What could the atomic numbers of X and Y be?

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 3 columns and 5 rows (including header).
Column 1: row letter (A–D)
Column 2: 'X'
Column 3: 'Y'
Row A: 3 | 1
Row B: 8 | 4
Row C: 11 | 7
Row D: 13 | 9
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

A  X=3, Y=1
B  X=8, Y=4
C  X=11, Y=7
D  X=13, Y=9

Which of the following reactions shows the amphoteric property of zinc oxide?

A  2ZnO + C → 2Zn + CO2
B  ZnO + Mg → MgO + Zn
C  ZnO + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2O
D  ZnO + 2NaOH → Na2ZnO2 + H2O

The following statements about dilute sulfuric acid are all correct.

1  It reacts with copper(II) oxide, forming a blue solution.
2  It turns anhydrous copper(II) sulfate from white to blue.
3  A white precipitate is formed when aqueous barium nitrate is added.
4  Addition of methyl orange shows that the solution has a pH value of less than 4.0.

Which two statements confirm the acidic nature of the solution?

A  1 and 2
B  1 and 4
C  2 and 3
D  3 and 4

A titration method can be used to prepare aqueous potassium sulfate from potassium carbonate and dilute sulfuric acid. Which of the following conclusions from this information is correct?

A  Potassium carbonate is an acidic salt.
B  Potassium carbonate is insoluble in water.
C  Potassium carbonate neutralises dilute sulfuric acid.
D  Potassium carbonate reacts more vigorously than sodium carbonate with dilute sulfuric acid.

Solid X is gradually added to aqueous solution Y. The changes in pH are shown in the graph below.

[DIAGRAM – pH GRAPH AND TABLE]
Line graph: y-axis 'pH' (0–14), x-axis 'mass of solid X added / g'. Curve starts near 0, rises gradually, then sharply through 7 and levels off near 7–8 (S-shaped neutralisation curve starting acidic).
Below the graph: a table with 3 columns and 5 rows (including header).
Column 1: row letter (A–D)
Column 2: 'X'
Column 3: 'Y'
Row A: potassium carbonate | ethanoic acid
Row B: potassium oxide | ethanoic acid
Row C: sodium oxide | hydrochloric acid
Row D: zinc oxide | hydrochloric acid
Recommended rendering tool: image generator for graph, SVG table for data.

What could X and Y be?

A  X = potassium carbonate, Y = ethanoic acid
B  X = potassium oxide, Y = ethanoic acid
C  X = sodium oxide, Y = hydrochloric acid
D  X = zinc oxide, Y = hydrochloric acid

An experiment was carried out to investigate the process of rusting in iron nails.

[DIAGRAM – THREE NAILS]
Three nails labelled X, Y and Z.
Nail X: iron nail wrapped with copper wire.
Nail Y: iron nail wrapped with zinc wire.
Nail Z: iron nail coated with copper (electroplated).
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

Which of the following statements is correct?

A  None of the nails rusted.
B  X rusted the fastest.
C  Y rusted the fastest.
D  Z rusted the fastest.

Element X is one of the components found in car fuels. It forms an oxide Y when burnt in car engines and gets further oxidised into Z when it is released in the atmosphere. Which of the following statements is true about the substances X, Y and Z?

A  Element X could be sulfur.
B  Substances X, Y and Z exist naturally as gases.
C  Substances Y and Z increase the pH of river water.
D  Substance Z binds irreversibly to haemoglobin in blood cells resulting in respiratory difficulties in humans.

Waste gases from a coal-burning power station are passed through powdered calcium carbonate to reduce pollution to the atmosphere.

Which waste gas will NOT be removed by the powdered calcium carbonate?

A  carbon dioxide
B  carbon monoxide
C  nitrogen dioxide
D  sulfur dioxide

Elements P, Q and R have the following properties:
• P reacts with Group 1 metals to form ionic compounds.
• Q reacts with oxygen to form compounds with giant covalent structures and very high melting and boiling points.
• R reacts violently with acids to give off hydrogen gas.

What is the arrangement order of these elements across a period in the Periodic Table?

A  P, Q, R
B  Q, R, P
C  R, P, Q
D  R, Q, P

Gaseous chlorine was passed through the apparatus set-up shown below. The apparatus was continuously heated throughout with a Bunsen flame.

[DIAGRAM – APPARATUS WITH TABLE]
Apparatus: U-tube containing potassium bromide (region 1), potassium chloride (region 2), and potassium iodide (region 3 at bottom), with cotton wool plug at exit (region 4). Chlorine gas enters at the left.
Below: a table with 5 columns and 5 rows (header + 4 answer rows) showing expected colours at each region.
Row A: brown gas | yellow-green gas | violet gas | yellow-green gas
Row B: violet gas | yellow-green gas | brown gas | violet gas
Row C: yellow-green gas | brown gas | violet gas | violet gas
Row D: yellow-green gas | brown gas | brown gas | brown gas
Recommended rendering tool: image generator for apparatus, SVG table for observations.

What would be the observations made at regions 1, 2, 3 and 4?

A  row A
B  row B
C  row C
D  row D

The following graph shows the change in reactant and product concentrations with time during a chemical reaction.

[DIAGRAM – CONCENTRATION vs TIME GRAPH]
Line graph with x-axis 'time (s)' and y-axis 'concentration (mol/dm³)'.
Three curves: X starts high and decreases to near zero (reactant); Y starts at zero and rises to highest level (major product); Z starts at zero and rises to an intermediate level (minor product).
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

Which equation represents the reaction shown in the graph?

A  X → Y + Z
B  X → 2Y + Z
C  Z → 2X + Y
D  Z → 2Y + X

Copper(II) sulfate reacts violently in excess magnesium powder to give magnesium sulfate and copper metal.

CuSO4 (aq) + Mg (s) → MgSO4 (aq) + Cu (s)    ΔH = −164 kJ/mol

Which of the following will be observed when 25 cm³ of 0.05 mol/dm³ copper(II) sulfate is reacted with 2 g of magnesium powder?

A  164 kJ of heat is absorbed in the reaction.
B  328 kJ of heat is released in the reaction.
C  The temperature of the solution increases.
D  The solution remains blue as there is insufficient magnesium powder.

Hydrogen peroxide solution is catalytically decomposed by manganese(IV) oxide to yield water and oxygen gas. Three experiments were performed using a fixed mass of catalyst but with:
(i)   50 cm³ of 2.0 mol/dm³ hydrogen peroxide
(ii)  100 cm³ of 1.0 mol/dm³ hydrogen peroxide
(iii) 100 cm³ of 2.0 mol/dm³ hydrogen peroxide

[DIAGRAM – LINE GRAPH AND TABLE]
Line graph with x-axis 'time' and y-axis 'total volume of oxygen evolved'. Three curves X, Y, Z with X reaching the highest plateau, Y and Z lower.
Below: a table mapping curves X, Y, Z to experiments (i), (ii), (iii).
Row A: X=(i), Y=(ii), Z=(iii)
Row B: X=(i), Y=(iii), Z=(ii) [wait - need to match by volume and concentration]
Row C: X=(iii), Y=(i) or (ii) combos
Row D: Z=(iii), Y=(ii), X=(i)
Recommended rendering tool: image generator for graph, SVG table.

On the graph above, which of the curves X, Y and Z relate to the solutions (i), (ii) and (iii)?

A  X=(i), Y=(ii), Z=(iii)
B  X=(i), Y=(iii), Z=(ii)
C  X=(iii), Y=(i), Z=(ii)
D  X=(iii), Y=(ii), Z=(i)

What happens when a current is drawn from the simple cell shown below?

[DIAGRAM – GALVANIC CELL]
A simple cell: zinc electrode on the left and copper electrode on the right, both immersed in aqueous sodium sulfate solution. A voltmeter (V) is connected at the top.
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

A  Copper electrode dissolves to form copper(II) ions.
B  Electrons flow from the copper to zinc electrode.
C  Hydrogen gas is liberated at the zinc electrode.
D  Zinc electrode dissolves to form zinc ions.

Which of the following statements about biofuel is true?

A  Biofuel can be separated by simple distillation.
B  Biofuel is an alternative fuel source to petroleum.
C  Biofuel is formed from the remains of dead animals.
D  Biofuel is the main feedstock for the petrochemical industry.
